author: Reichsarchiv
title: Der Weltkrieg 1914 bis 1918. Die militärischen Operationen zu Lande, Band 3: Der Marne-Feldzug — Von der Sambre zur Marne
notes: German official history, the volume between the frontier battles and the Marne: the operations of the German western armies from the Sambre to the Marne, roughly 23 August to 4 September 1914. It names, day by day and in its own words, the town each Armee-Oberkommando moved its Hauptquartier to, which is this pack's citation for the German commander tracks over the advance; it also carries the move of the Große Hauptquartier from Koblenz to Luxembourg on the morning of 30 August (p. 190). It also prints in full the German texts of three of this pack's Document cards, which were previously cited to Bd. 1 or Bd. 4 in error: the OHL 'Allgemeine Anweisungen an die 1. bis 7. Armee für den Fortgang der Operationen' of 27 August (pp. 7–9, with the assessment of the enemy on p. 4), the Bülow–Kluck wireless exchange of 30 August from both ends (pp. 137 and 177), and the OHL signal to the First and Second Armies of the evening of 4 September (p. 311), which the volume dates 'in der achten Abendstunde'. Bd. 4, which would carry the battle itself, the Hentsch report and Moltke's tour of 11 September, is not digitised. Apologetic on command decisions, like Bd. 1, and it measures the campaign by what the German army did. Chapter 12, 'Die Vorgänge in Belgien bis zum 7. September' (pp. 327–332), is this pack's citation for the IX. Reservekorps after its release from Schleswig: still on the railway to Tirlemont on 25 August, detraining through Louvain, delayed there by the rising of the 26th, and over the Willebroek canal on 30 August with one brigade left to garrison Brussels. Read at page resolution for the battle of St. Quentin (Guise), which Bd. 1 cannot cover: pp. 145–179 carry it corps by corps — the fight for the Oise crossing at Guise on 28 August and Emmich's X. Corps taking the bridges and the town in the fifth hour of the afternoon (p. 147); the X. Corps' 5 p.m. report and the 1st Army's message that it had forced the Somme at Cléry–St. Christ (p. 151); the X. Reserve Corps west of the Oise on the 29th (p. 153); the VII. Corps' 14th Division over the Somme at Ham (p. 153); the cavalry corps at Libermont and Cugny (p. 159); the X. Corps at Mont d'Origny (p. 161); the Guard Corps at Voulpaix (p. 163); the orders for the 30th (pp. 167–169); and where the whole army went to rest on the evening of the 30th (p. 179). pp. 137–143 carry the 1st Army's left wheel past the battle.
